chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Ahmad narrated to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Muslim, from a man from our companions who is nicknamed Sikbaj, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nasr, the master of the Atrak, and he was in charge of some of the affairs of the Imam (peace be upon him), who said:
He said one day, and he dictated it to me from the Book of Ringing/Sealing: 'Wearing the emerald ring is ease; there is no hardship in it.'

key_terms.التَّخَتُّمِ: The act of wearing a ring or sealing with a ring
key_terms.صَاحِبِ الْأَتْرَاکِ: Master of the Atrak (a title indicating a specific role or office)

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of wearing an emerald ring according to Imam Musa al-Kadhim (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Thawab al-Amal*, Imam Musa al-Kadhim (peace be upon him) dictates that wearing an emerald ring signifies 'ease' (yusr) without 'hardship' (usqr), reflecting the Shia tradition of attributing spiritual tranquility and divine favor to specific adornments. This practice is rooted in the belief that such items serve as tangible reminders of God’s blessings, aligning with the broader Islamic emphasis on permissible beauty and modesty.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1.  It is narrated from Imam Musa Kadhim (a.s.) who read out from  a  book:  “There  are  lots  of  comforts  for  a  person wearing the Emerald ring and there is no hardship for him.” The narrator wrote down these words of Imam (a.s.).
